prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name one single “best” lawyer — the best choice depends on the details of your case and which attorney’s experience, resources and style match your needs. I can, however, tell you what to look for and help you find strong candidates in Dallas.

What to look for in a truck-accident lawyer
- Trucking-specific experience: look for lawyers who regularly handle 18-wheeler/CMV cases (not just general car crashes). Trucking cases involve federal/state trucking regs (FMCSA), carrier investigations, ELD/black-box data, and multiple potential defendants (driver, motor carrier, owner, maintenance companies, insurers).
- Trial experience and large-case results: trucking cases often require substantial resources and expert witnesses; check for verdicts/settlements and whether the attorney tries cases if needed.
- Resources and team: investigators, accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and ability to take uninsured/underinsured or aggressive carriers through litigation.
- Credentials & recognition: board certification in personal injury trial law (if applicable), AV Preeminent/Martindale-Hubbell ratings, Super Lawyers, Million Dollar Advocates membership, or similar.
- Communication & service: clear fee structure (usually contingency), responsiveness, and a readable engagement agreement.
- Local Dallas/Texas experience: knowledge of state law, local judges, and regional trucking companies/insurance practices.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many truck cases have you handled? What were the results?
- Do you regularly handle 18-wheeler cases and try cases to verdict?
- Who will handle day-to-day work — you or a team member?
- What experts would you expect to retain?
- How are fees and costs handled (contingency percentage, who advances costs)?
- How long do you estimate my case will take?
- Can you provide references or client reviews?

Evidence and documents to bring to initial meetings
- Police report and crash photos
- Contact info for all drivers/witnesses
- Medical records and bills, hospitalization records
- Insurance information
- Any correspondence with insurers
- Vehicle photos and damage estimates
- Dates and description of injuries/treatment

Red flags
- No trucking-specific experience
- Reluctance to discuss trial experience or past results
- Poor communication during the consult
- No clear fee agreement or evasive answers about costs

How I can help next
- I can pull a short list of well-regarded Dallas truck-accident attorneys or firms if you’d like names and contact info. Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and a few case details (date of crash, severity of injuries, whether police report exists), and I’ll prepare a short tailored list and suggested questions for each firm.

Would you like me to find specific lawyers in Dallas for you? If so, please share your ZIP code and any key case facts.
